recommendation: Indicate the design in the title or abstract
study_response: Title and abstract identify this as a national secret-shopper (audit) study.

recommendation: Balanced summary of what was done and found
study_response: Structured abstract reports the service menu as primary and states that the access comparison was uninformative.

recommendation: Scientific background and rationale
study_response: RRM service scope determines which patients can be served; national data were previously absent.

recommendation: State specific objectives and any prespecified hypotheses
study_response: Primary: define the service menu. Secondary and exploratory: access by caller scenario. No power analysis was prespecified in the protocol; achieved precision is reported instead.

recommendation: Present key elements of study design early
study_response: Cross-sectional audit; each practice eligible for one call per scenario.

recommendation: Setting, locations, and relevant dates
study_response: United States, 2025-2026; RRM practices compiled from professional directories.

recommendation: Eligibility criteria and selection
study_response: National roster of RRM practices; call dispositions mapped to standard access-audit exclusion codes.

recommendation: Define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, confounders
study_response: Primary outcome: reported service menu. Secondary: appointment availability inferred from call documentation, strict and broad definitions. Reached and offer-eligible are distinct denominators.

recommendation: Sources of data and measurement
study_response: Trained callers using standardized scripts; responses entered in REDCap (pid 39546).

recommendation: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias
study_response: Within-practice matched design for the secondary outcome; caller-overlap analysis reports which contrasts can be separated from caller effects; duplicate practice-scenario cells handled by a prespecified rule with first-vs-last sensitivity.

recommendation: Explain how the study size was arrived at
study_response: No a priori sample-size calculation was performed. The achievable sample was the national roster of RRM practices. Minimum detectable effects are reported for every paired contrast.

recommendation: Explain how quantitative variables were handled
study_response: Proportions with 95% Wilson or Clopper-Pearson intervals; wait time in business days, log-transformed and reported as geometric mean ratios.

recommendation: Statistical methods, subgroups, missing data, sensitivity
study_response: Exact McNemar for matched contrasts; mixed-effects logistic regression with practice random intercept; two-part hurdle model for wait; Mantel-Haenszel stratification where caller overlap permits. Missingness by arm reported in Appendix Table S2.

recommendation: Report numbers at each stage
study_response: 234 calls placed, 108 reached a live office, 98 completed the service interview; Figures 2 and 3.

recommendation: Characteristics of study participants
study_response: Practice-level characteristics and per-scenario cascade in Table 1 and Figure 3.

recommendation: Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures
study_response: Service prevalences in Figure 1 and Appendix Table S3.

recommendation: Give unadjusted and, if applicable, adjusted estimates with precision
study_response: All estimates reported with 95% confidence intervals. P-values are not reported for the exploratory access contrasts, with the reason stated in the text.

recommendation: Report other analyses done
study_response: Strict vs broad availability, first-vs-last duplicate-call sensitivity, caller-stratified Mantel-Haenszel estimate.

recommendation: Summarise key results with reference to objectives
study_response: Primary finding is the structural absence of donor-gamete and ART services.

recommendation: Discuss limitations, including bias and imprecision
study_response: Derived availability outcome; caller-scenario confounding with no within-caller information for two of three contrasts; documentation completeness differing by arm; low reachability; single call per scenario.

recommendation: Cautious overall interpretation
study_response: The service finding is stated as structural; the access comparison is stated as uninformative rather than null.

recommendation: Generalisability
study_response: Findings describe the reachable subset of RRM practices nationally.

recommendation: Give the source of funding
study_response: No external funding; COMIRB 25-2596.
